metadata.title: Research Involving Children as Subjects and Not Otherwise Approvable by an Institutional Review Board: Process for Referrals to Food and Drug Administration and Office for Human Research Protections: Draft Guidance for Institutional Review Boards, Investigators, and Sponsors
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 48 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 49 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 50 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 51 not required. 52
candidates.context: This guidance is intended to assist institutional review boards (IRBs), institutions, investigators, 42 and sponsors in understanding the processes used for review of research involving children as 43 subjects that is not otherwise approvable by an IRB and has been referred to the Food and Drug 44 Administration (FDA) under 21 CFR 50.54, the Office for Human Research Protections (OHRP) 45 under 45 CFR 46.407, or both, for review. 46

candidates.statement: For multisite research regulated by FDA and conducted under an IND or IDE, if an IRB makes 449 a referral under 21 CFR 50.54, FDA will determine whether the clinical investigation may 450 proceed (or continue, if enrollment has already begun at one or more sites) or will be placed on 451 clinical hold. 19 In the case of a referral regarding an investigation for which an IDE application 452 (or supplement) is pending, FDA may also consider other actions. 20 If FDA concludes that a 453 clinical hold is appropriate, the agency generally intends to apply that clinical hold to all sites, 454 regardless of whether IRBs other than the one that referred the protocol have approved the 455 protocol. While the 21 CFR 50.54 review is underway, FDA will inform the sponsor whether 456 the clinical investigation has been placed on clinical hold and the sponsor must then notify 457 investigators if the clinical investigation has been placed on clinical hold. 21 The sponsor also 458 should inform the other study site IRBs. 22
